_comment: Candidate underlyings for the Massive (ex-Polygon) options snapshot endpoint.
Two fields matter and they come from different places. 'exercise' is a fact
about the contract, from the exchange's specifications -- it does not depend
on any data plan, and it decides whether this project can price the thing at
all. 'available' is a fact about YOUR subscription and cannot be known from
here; run dashboard/diagnose.py to fill it in.
Only 'european' contracts can be validated against Black, calibrated with
parity-implied forwards, or priced by the Monte Carlo engine as-is. American
ones need the LSM engine, a dividend forecast and a borrow estimate, because
put-call parity degrades to an inequality and the forward can no longer be

endpoint_conventions.note: The prefix rule differs by endpoint family and is a common source of empty results.

candidates.name: S&P 500 (AM-settled)
candidates.note: The primary target. Deep, liquid, and the reference case for parity forwards.

candidates.name: S&P 500 weeklies (PM)
candidates.note: Separate root from SPX; often where the liquidity actually is.

candidates.name: Mini-SPX (1/10 SPX)
candidates.note: Same index, smaller notional. Thinner book.

candidates.name: S&P 100 (European)
candidates.note: The European twin of OEX -- note the pair below.

candidates.name: Volatility Index
candidates.note: European exercise, but the underlying is a forward-starting variance object, not a tradable spot. Parity-implied forwards do NOT mean what they mean elsewhere. Out of scope for this project.

candidates.name: S&P 100 (American)
candidates.note: The trap: an INDEX option that is American-exercise. Its European twin is XEO. Do not assume index implies European.

candidates.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF
candidates.note: The most liquid options in the world, and unusable here without LSM plus a dividend forecast. Useful only to prove the endpoint and plan work.

candidates.name: Apple
candidates.note: A single name, for the Phase B/C path once borrow and dividends are handled.
